objects.definition:
#if !defined(__MACTYPES__)
typedef unsigned char  Byte;  /* 8 bits */
#endif
#ifdef SMALL_MEDIUM
#  define Bytef Byte FAR
#else
   typedef Byte  FAR Bytef;
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned 8-bit byte type used by zlib APIs. Bytef is the far-pointer-qualified alias on segmented models or simply Byte with FAR applied elsewhere.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned int   uInt;  /* 16 bits or more */
typedef uInt  FAR uIntf;
objects.description: Unsigned integer type used by the API for counts and lengths. Guaranteed to be at least 16 bits. uIntf is the FAR-qualified alias.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned long  uLong; /* 32 bits or more */
typedef uLong FAR uLongf;
objects.description: Unsigned long integer type used by the API for sizes and totals. At least 32 bits. uLongf is the FAR-qualified alias.

objects.definition: typedef char  FAR charf;
objects.description: Char type with FAR qualification for segmented memory models. Used in some legacy interfaces.

objects.definition: typedef int   FAR intf;
objects.description: Int type with FAR qualification for segmented memory models. Rarely used directly.
Pointer-to-const-void type used in the API for read-only buffers. Always use pointer form when passing to functions.
Generic pointer type (possibly FAR-qualified) used for opaque pointers and allocator interfaces.
Generic pointer type used widely in the API for untyped buffers and opaque values.

objects.definition:
#ifdef Z_SOLO
#  ifdef _WIN64
     typedef unsigned long long z_size_t;
#  else
     typedef unsigned long z_size_t;
#  endif
#else
#  define z_longlong long long
#  if defined(NO_SIZE_T)
     typedef unsigned NO_SIZE_T z_size_t;
#  elif defined(STDC)
#    include <stddef.h>
     typedef size_t z_size_t;
#  else
     typedef unsigned long z_size_t;
#  endif
#  undef z_longlong
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned size type used by some zlib APIs that mirrors size_t where available, otherwise an unsigned integer large enough for pointer size.
Unsigned integer type used for CRC tables and CRC computations in zlib. Width is 32 bits where possible.

objects.definition:
#ifndef z_off_t
#  define z_off_t long long
#endif
objects.description: Signed offset type used by zlib for file offsets and lengths in some APIs. It is defined as long long unless overridden by platform headers earlier in zconf.h.

objects.definition:
#if !defined(_WIN32) && defined(Z_LARGE64)
#  define z_off64_t off64_t
#elif defined(__MINGW32__)
#  define z_off64_t long long
#elif defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__GNUC__)
#  define z_off64_t __int64
#elif defined(__GO32__)
#  define z_off64_t offset_t
#else
#  define z_off64_t z_off_t
#endif
objects.description: Signed 64-bit (or wider) offset type used when large-file support is enabled. Alias resolves to a platform-specific 64-bit offset type or to z_off_t otherwise.

objects.definition: typedef voidpf (*alloc_func)(voidpf opaque, uInt items, uInt size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory allocation callbacks used by z_stream. Returns a pointer to allocated memory for items*size bytes.

objects.definition: typedef void   (*free_func)(voidpf opaque, voidpf address);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory free callbacks paired with alloc_func in z_stream.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned (*in_func)(void FAR *,
                            z_const unsigned char FAR * FAR *);
objects.description: Callback type used by inflateBack() to supply input. Returns number of bytes available and provides a pointer to the buffer via an out-parameter.

objects.definition: typedef int (*out_func)(void FAR *, unsigned char FAR *, unsigned);
objects.description: Callback type used by inflateBack() to consume output. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.

objects.definition: struct internal_state;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared internal zlib state structure used by z_stream. Not defined in the public header; managed internally by zlib.

objects.definition:
typedef struct z_stream_s {
    z_const Bytef *next_in;     /* next input byte */
    uInt     avail_in;  /* number of bytes available at next_in */
    uLong    total_in;  /* total number of input bytes read so far */

    Bytef    *next_out; /* next output byte will go here */
    uInt     avail_out; /* remaining free space at next_out */
    uLong    total_out; /* total number of bytes output so far */

    z_const char *msg;  /* last error message, NULL if no error */
    struct internal_state FAR *state; /* not visible by applications */

    alloc_func zalloc;  /* used to allocate the internal state */
    free_func  zfree;   /* used to free the internal state */
    voidpf     opaque;  /* private data object passed to zalloc and zfree */

    int     data_type;  /* best guess about the data type: binary or text
                           for deflate, or the decoding state for inflate */
    uLong   adler;      /* Adler-32 or CRC-32 value of the uncompressed data */
    uLong   reserved;   /* reserved for future use */
} z_stream;

typedef z_stream FAR *z_streamp;
objects.description: Primary stream state structure for all deflate/inflate operations. Holds I/O buffer pointers, counters, error message, allocator hooks, and internal state pointer. Users must set zalloc, zfree, and opaque before initialization functions. Lifetime is owned by the application; internal_state is managed by zlib.

objects.definition:
typedef struct gz_header_s {
    int     text;       /* true if compressed data believed to be text */
    uLong   time;       /* modification time */
    int     xflags;     /* extra flags (not used when writing a gzip file) */
    int     os;         /* operating system */
    Bytef   *extra;     /* pointer to extra field or Z_NULL if none */
    uInt    extra_len;  /* extra field length (valid if extra != Z_NULL) */
    uInt    extra_max;  /* space at extra (only when reading header) */
    Bytef   *name;      /* pointer to zero-terminated file name or Z_NULL */
    uInt    name_max;   /* space at name (only when reading header) */
    Bytef   *comment;   /* pointer to zero-terminated comment or Z_NULL */
    uInt    comm_max;   /* space at comment (only when reading header) */
    int     hcrc;       /* true if there was or will be a header crc */
    int     done;       /* true when done reading gzip header (not used
                           when writing a gzip file) */
} gz_header;

typedef gz_header FAR *gz_headerp;
objects.description: Structure used to communicate gzip header metadata to and from the API. Used with deflateSetHeader() and inflateGetHeader(). Pointers must reference buffers provided by the application.

Opaque handle type for zlib's gz* file API. It is a pointer to an internal struct with a minimal exposed subset used by the gzgetc macro; applications should treat it as opaque and obtain instances via gzopen/gzdopen.

functions.name: zlibVersion
functions.description: Returns the zlib library version string compiled into the library. Typically compared to the header’s ZLIB_VERSION to ensure ABI/API match. Used implicitly by deflateInit/inflateInit via macros.
requirements: No arguments; returns const pointer that must not be modified.
Caller may compare first character with ZLIB_VERSION to check compatibility.

functions.name: deflate
functions.description: Incrementally compresses input from strm->next_in into strm->next_out according to the flush directive. Advances next_in/avail_in and next_out/avail_out. Can be called repeatedly until completion.
requirements: strm must be a valid stream returned by deflateInit/deflateInit2/deflateReset.
Before each call, ensure at least one of: avail_in > 0 or avail_out > 0.
If avail_out is 0 and deflate returns Z_OK, caller must provide more output space and call again with the same flush until non-zero avail_out.
flush must be one of Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FULL_FLUSH, Z_FINISH, or Z_BLOCK.
For single-call compression, set avail_out >= deflateBound() and flush=Z_FINISH to guarantee Z_STREAM_END.
When using Z_FULL_FLUSH or Z_SYNC_FLUSH, ensure avail_out > 6 when starting the flush to avoid repeated markers.
next_in must be non-NULL when avail_in > 0; next_out must be non-NULL when avail_out > 0.
Returns Z_OK on progress, Z_STREAM_END on completion with Z_FINISH, Z_BUF_ERROR if no progress possible, Z_STREAM_ERROR on bad state, Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure.

functions.name: deflateEnd
functions.description: Frees all dynamically allocated compression state for the stream. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream previously initialized.
After Z_STREAM_END from deflate(), only deflateReset/deflateEnd are allowed; call deflateEnd to free.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state invalid, Z_DATA_ERROR if freed prematurely (input/output discarded).

functions.name: inflate
functions.description: Incrementally decompresses data from strm->next_in to strm->next_out. Advances pointers and sizes. Supports zlib, gzip, or raw streams depending on initialization.
requirements: strm must be initialized by inflateInit/inflateInit2/inflateReset.
Before each call, ensure at least one of: avail_in > 0 or avail_out > 0.
To complete in one call, use flush=Z_FINISH and provide output large enough for all uncompressed data.
If inflate returns Z_OK with avail_out == 0, provide more output and call again.
flush must be one of Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FINISH, Z_BLOCK, or Z_TREES.
If Z_BLOCK/Z_TREES are used, caller should examine strm->data_type for block-boundary/bit info.
If Z_NEED_DICT is returned, provide the preset dictionary via inflateSetDictionary() before continuing.
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_END, Z_NEED_DICT, Z_DATA_ERROR, Z_STREAM_ERROR, Z_MEM_ERROR, or Z_BUF_ERROR as documented.
next_in must be non-NULL if avail_in > 0; next_out must be non-NULL if avail_out > 0.

functions.name: inflateEnd
functions.description: Frees all dynamically allocated decompression state for the stream. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream previously initialized.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state invalid.

functions.name: deflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int deflateSetDictionary(z_streamp strm, const Bytef *dictionary, uInt dictLength);
functions.description: Sets an initial compression dictionary to improve compression of short or predictable data. Updates strm->adler to the Adler-32 of the dictionary (not for raw).
requirements: strm must be initialized for deflate.
dictionary must not be Z_NULL; dictLength is the number of dictionary bytes.
For zlib format: call immediately after deflateInit/deflateInit2/deflateReset and before any deflate().
For raw deflate: call before any deflate(), or exactly at a block boundary immediately after completing a block (after consuming all input and output).
Effective usable dictionary may be limited to window size minus 262 bytes.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameter or wrong stream state.

functions.name: deflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieves the current sliding window dictionary maintained by deflate into the provided buffer and/or length.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
If dictionary != Z_NULL, it must point to a buffer large enough; 32768 bytes is always enough.
If dictionary == Z_NULL, only *dictLength is set; if dictLength == Z_NULL, length is not returned.
Returned length can be less than window size (up to 258 bytes less).
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state inconsistent.

functions.name: deflateCopy
functions.description: Makes dest a complete duplicate of source deflate stream, including internal state, to branch compression with different strategies.
requirements: source must be a valid initialized deflate stream.
dest must be a valid z_stream struct (zalloc/zfree may be used); enough memory must be available.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure, Z_STREAM_ERROR if source state is inconsistent (e.g., zalloc is Z_NULL).
After use, free duplicated streams with deflateEnd().

functions.name: deflateReset
functions.description: Resets a deflate stream as if deflateEnd followed by deflateInit, but reuses the internal state allocation and preserves attributes like level/strategy. Resets total_in/total_out/adler/msg.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream with zalloc/state set.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state (e.g., zalloc or state is Z_NULL).

functions.name: deflateParams
functions.signature: int deflateParams(z_streamp strm, int level, int strategy);
functions.description: Dynamically changes compression level and strategy for an active deflate stream. May emit a Z_BLOCK internally to complete pending input under old parameters.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
level and strategy as defined for deflateInit2().
If an internal deflate(Z_BLOCK) lacks output space, parameters will not change; caller may retry with more output space.
For guaranteed parameter change: flush using deflate(Z_BLOCK or similar) until avail_out != 0, provide no more input, then call deflateParams().
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream/parameters, Z_BUF_ERROR if insufficient output space to complete transition (parameters unchanged).

functions.name: deflateTune
functions.signature: int deflateTune(z_streamp strm, int good_length, int max_lazy, int nice_length, int max_chain);
functions.description: Fine-tunes internal string-matching parameters used by deflate. For expert/optimization use only.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream, after deflateInit/deflateInit2.
Parameters are algorithmic tunables; meanings per zlib’s deflate implementation.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream.

functions.name: deflateBound
functions.description: Returns an upper bound on the compressed size for sourceLen bytes with the current stream settings (and after deflateSetHeader if used). Useful to preallocate output for single-pass deflate.
requirements: strm must be initialized by deflateInit/deflateInit2; call after deflateSetHeader() if used.
sourceLen is the amount of input that will be provided to that first deflate().
If first deflate() is called with those sourceLen bytes, output buffer sized to deflateBound(), and flush=Z_FINISH, deflate() is guaranteed to return Z_STREAM_END.

functions.name: deflatePending
functions.description: Reports the number of pending whole bytes and additional bits not yet provided to the application due to limited output space.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
pending or bits may be Z_NULL to skip setting those outputs; otherwise they must be valid writable pointers.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent stream.

functions.name: deflateUsed
functions.description: Returns in *bits the number of deflate bits (1..8) used in the last byte when flushing to a byte boundary; 0 if none yet. Helps locate last bit of a deflate stream.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
bits must be a valid pointer.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream.

functions.name: deflatePrime
functions.signature: int deflatePrime(z_streamp strm, int bits, int value);
functions.description: Inserts up to 16 least-significant bits of value into the deflate output bitstream prior to the first deflate() call (raw only). Used to append streams bit-aligned.
requirements: strm must be initialized with deflateInit2()/deflateReset() for raw deflate; must be called before the first deflate() after init/reset.
bits must be 0..16; value’s least-significant 'bits' bits are used.
Returns Z_OK, Z_BUF_ERROR if insufficient internal buffer room, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream.

functions.name: deflateSetHeader
functions.description: Provides gzip header metadata to be emitted when output format was requested as gzip in deflateInit2(). Sets fields from gz_header (xflags ignored).
requirements: strm must be initialized with deflateInit2() requesting gzip, or reset via deflateReset().
Call before the first deflate() after init/reset.
If head->name/comment are non-NULL they must be zero-terminated; if extra != Z_NULL, extra_len bytes must be available.
If head->hcrc is true, a header CRC is included.
Returns Z_OK or Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream.

functions.name: inflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int inflateSetDictionary(z_streamp strm, const Bytef *dictionary, uInt dictLength);
functions.description: Supplies the decompression dictionary requested by inflate() after Z_NEED_DICT, or sets/augments dictionary for raw inflate at any time.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
If responding to Z_NEED_DICT, provide the exact dictionary used by compressor (identified by strm->adler).
dictionary must not be Z_NULL; dictLength is its size.
For raw inflate, may be called at any time; if smaller than window and window has data, it augments existing window.
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters/state, Z_DATA_ERROR if dictionary Adler-32 mismatch.

functions.name: inflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieves the current sliding dictionary from inflate into buffer and/or returns its length.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
If dictionary != Z_NULL, it must have space for up to 32768 bytes.
If dictionary == Z_NULL, only length is returned; if dictLength == Z_NULL, length is not returned.
Returns Z_OK, or Z_STREAM_ERROR for inconsistent stream state.

functions.name: inflateSync
functions.description: Skips invalid compressed data to the next possible Z_FULL_FLUSH point (00 00 FF FF) without producing output, to attempt resynchronization.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream with input provided.
May return Z_OK when a candidate flush point is found, Z_BUF_ERROR if no more input, Z_DATA_ERROR if not found, or Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream invalid.
On success, total_in indicates where valid data was found.

functions.name: inflateCopy
functions.description: Duplicates an inflate stream state into dest, useful for random access checkpoints.
requirements: source must be a valid initialized inflate stream.
dest must be a z_stream ready to receive copied state; sufficient memory required.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure, Z_STREAM_ERROR if source invalid (e.g., zalloc is Z_NULL).

functions.name: inflateReset
functions.description: Resets an inflate stream state as if inflateEnd+inflateInit, preserving attributes from inflateInit2. Resets totals/adler/msg.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: inflateReset2
functions.description: Resets inflate stream and optionally changes wrap/window requests as per inflateInit2 semantics. Frees window if size changes; reallocated on demand.
requirements: strm must be valid.
windowBits as for inflateInit2 (8..15, negative for raw, >15 for gzip/zlib auto per docs).
Returns Z_OK, or Z_STREAM_ERROR for invalid stream or windowBits.

functions.name: inflatePrime
functions.signature: int inflatePrime(z_streamp strm, int bits, int value);
functions.description: Inserts up to 16 bits into the inflate input bit buffer prior to consuming bytes from next_in, typically to align to mid-byte starts or after Z_BLOCK boundaries.
requirements: strm must be initialized for raw inflate (inflateInit2()/inflateReset()) and used before the first inflate() call; also allowed after inflate returns at block/header boundary with Z_BLOCK.
bits must be <= 16; negative bits empties the input bit buffer.
If in the middle of header/trailer/stored lengths, only eight bits may be available; then bits > 8 is out of range.
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid state/arguments.

functions.name: inflateMark
functions.description: Returns a packed value encoding inflate’s current code-processing position: lower 16 bits are bytes already emitted for current code; upper bits indicate either -1 with state (0 or non-zero) or distance in bits back to current code. Used for random access bookkeeping.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Returns -65536 on inconsistent stream state.

functions.name: inflateGetHeader
functions.description: Requests that gzip header fields be stored into the provided gz_header during inflate. head->done indicates completion; -1 indicates zlib stream.
requirements: Call after inflateInit2()/inflateReset() and before first inflate().
head’s extra/name/comment pointers must be either Z_NULL or point to buffers sized by extra_max/name_max/comm_max.
On completion, extra_len is set, and pointers may be set to Z_NULL if not present; strings may be truncated if buffers too small (no terminating zero implies truncation).
Returns Z_OK or Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream.

functions.name: inflateBack
functions.signature: int inflateBack(z_streamp strm, in_func in, void *in_desc, out_func out, void *out_desc);
functions.description: Performs a one-shot raw inflate using callback functions for input and output, typically to avoid extra copies by writing directly out of the sliding window.
requirements: Call inflateBackInit() first with a 32K (windowBits=15) window for general deflate streams (smaller only if certain input used small windows).
strm->next_in may point to initial input with avail_in set; otherwise in() will be called.
in() must return number of bytes available and set *buf; return 0 to indicate no input (inflateBack will return Z_BUF_ERROR).
out() must write len bytes from buf and return 0 on success; non-zero signals error and stops inflation.
Neither in() nor out() may modify the provided window buffer.
Returns Z_STREAM_END on success, Z_BUF_ERROR on in/out callback issues, Z_DATA_ERROR on stream errors (strm->msg set), Z_STREAM_ERROR if not properly initialized.

functions.name: inflateBackEnd
functions.description: Frees all memory allocated by inflateBackInit() for the stream.
requirements: strm must have been initialized by inflateBackInit().
Returns Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid stream state.

functions.name: zlibCompileFlags
functions.description: Returns a bitfield describing compile-time options, type sizes, and configuration of the zlib library (see documented bit layout).
requirements: No arguments; return value is a bitfield per documented layout.

functions.name: compress
functions.signature: int compress(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen);
functions.description: Convenience function to compress a full buffer in one step using default compression level. Writes compressed data to dest and sets *destLen to actual output size.
requirements: dest must point to output buffer with initial *destLen >= compressBound(sourceLen).
source/sourceLen specify input data.
On return, *destLen is set to compressed size.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure, Z_BUF_ERROR if dest not large enough.

functions.name: compress2
functions.signature: int compress2(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen, int level);
functions.description: Like compress(), but caller specifies compression level (Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or 0..9).
requirements: dest must have capacity >= compressBound(sourceLen); *destLen initially set to capacity.
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or 0..9.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_BUF_ERROR, or Z_STREAM_ERROR for invalid level.

functions.name: compressBound
functions.description: Returns an upper bound on compressed size for compress/compress2 of sourceLen bytes.
requirements: sourceLen is the uncompressed length; return value can be used to size dest buffer.

functions.name: uncompress
functions.signature: int uncompress(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen);
functions.description: Decompresses a full buffer in one step into dest. Requires dest to be big enough for the entire uncompressed data (length supplied out-of-band).
requirements: dest must point to buffer with capacity >= full uncompressed size; *destLen initially set to that capacity.
source/sourceLen specify the entire compressed input.
On return, *destLen is set to actual uncompressed size.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_BUF_ERROR if dest too small (partial data may be written), or Z_DATA_ERROR for invalid/incomplete input.

functions.name: uncompress2
functions.signature: int uncompress2(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong *sourceLen);
functions.description: Like uncompress(), but takes and returns the number of source bytes consumed via *sourceLen.
requirements: *destLen initially set to dest capacity; dest must be large enough for full uncompressed data.
*sourceLen initially set to available compressed bytes; on return it is updated to bytes consumed.
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_BUF_ERROR, or Z_DATA_ERROR.

functions.name: gzdopen
functions.description: Associates a gzFile stream with an existing file descriptor for gzip read/decompress or compress/write using mode like gzopen().
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor (not -1).

mode must begin with 'r', 'w', or 'a'; '+' is invalid. Optional flags: compression level (w), strategy letters (f,h,R,F), 'T' (transparent write/append), 'G' (disable transparent read), 'N' (non-blocking), 'e' (close-on-exec).
On success, subsequent gzclose will also close fd. If keeping original fd open, dup() it before calling gzdopen.
Returns NULL on invalid mode, fd == -1, or memory allocation failure.

functions.name: gzbuffer
functions.description: Sets the internal buffer size for a gzFile before I/O begins. Affects performance and gzprintf limit.
requirements: Must be called after gzopen()/gzdopen() and before any read/write on file.
size is requested internal buffer size (default 8192).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (e.g., called too late).

functions.name: gzsetparams
functions.signature: int gzsetparams(gzFile file, int level, int strategy);
functions.description: Changes compression level and/or strategy for an open gzFile being written. Flushes pending data before applying changes.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
level/strategy as in deflateInit2().
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR if not writable, Z_ERRNO on write error, Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure.

functions.name: gzread
functions.signature: int gzread(gzFile file, voidp buf, unsigned len);
functions.description: Reads and decompresses up to len uncompressed bytes into buf. Transparently reads plain files if not gzip. Supports concatenated gzip members and non-blocking reads.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
buf must be a valid buffer of at least len bytes.
Returns number of uncompressed bytes read (0 for EOF), or -1 on error. If len doesn’t fit in int, returns -1 and reads nothing.
For non-blocking or concurrent write sources, may return -1 with errno=EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK; use gzclearerr() to retry when appropriate.

functions.name: gzfread
functions.signature: z_size_t gzfread(voidp buf, z_size_t size, z_size_t nitems, gzFile file);
functions.description: fread-like interface to read and decompress up to nitems of size bytes. Returns count of full items read.
requirements: buf must have space for size*nitems bytes; if size*nitems overflows z_size_t, returns 0 and sets error state to Z_STREAM_ERROR.
file must be opened for reading.
On EOF with partial trailing item (size != 1), last partial item is read and EOF set; length not returned.

functions.name: gzwrite
functions.signature: int gzwrite(gzFile file, voidpc buf, unsigned len);
functions.description: Compresses and writes len uncompressed bytes from buf to file. Returns number of bytes accepted (may be < len on non-blocking writes) or 0 on error/len==0.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
If len doesn’t fit in int, returns 0 and writes nothing.

functions.name: gzfwrite
functions.signature: z_size_t gzfwrite(voidpc buf, z_size_t size, z_size_t nitems, gzFile file);
functions.description: fwrite-like interface to compress and write nitems of size bytes. Returns number of full items written.
requirements: If size*nitems overflows z_size_t, writes nothing, returns 0, sets error Z_STREAM_ERROR.
For concurrent-read or non-blocking writes, use size==1 to avoid partial-item ambiguity; otherwise partial item could be written with unknown extent.

functions.name: gzprintf
functions.description: fprintf-like formatting, conversion, compression, and write to gzFile. Returns number of uncompressed bytes actually written, or negative zlib error code.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.

Maximum uncompressed write is min(8191, gzbuffer size - 1); exceeding this returns 0 and writes nothing; risk of buffer overflow only if zlib compiled without snprintf/vsnprintf (see zlibCompileFlags).
On non-blocking stall, may return Z_BUF_ERROR and write nothing.

functions.name: gzputs
functions.description: Writes the null-terminated string s (excluding the terminator) to gzFile after compressing. Returns number of chars written or -1 on error.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
If string length doesn’t fit in int, returns -1 and writes nothing.

functions.name: gzgets
functions.signature: char * gzgets(gzFile file, char *buf, int len);
functions.description: Reads up to len-1 bytes or through a newline into buf, null-terminating on success. Returns buf on success, NULL on EOF or error (may return data read before error).
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
If no characters read (EOF) or len < 1, buf is untouched.
May break lines when reading non-blocking or concurrently written files; caller may need to reassemble.

functions.name: gzputc
functions.description: Writes a single byte (unsigned char converted from c) to gzFile after compression. Returns the value written or -1 on error.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.

functions.name: gzgetc
functions.description: Reads and decompresses a single byte. Returns the byte [0..255] or -1 on EOF/error. May be a macro that uses a small lookahead buffer for speed.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
When used as macro, it does minimal checking (doesn’t validate NULL or structure).
On non-blocking stall with no data, returns -1 and sets errno=EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK (use gzread() to continue).

functions.name: gzungetc
functions.description: Pushes back one byte onto the input stream to be returned by the next read. Returns the pushed character, or -1 on failure.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
c must not be -1; may fail if a character is already pushed and not yet read.
Pushed characters are discarded on gzseek()/gzrewind().
Calling gzungetc(-1,file) forces any pending seek to execute.

functions.name: gzflush
functions.description: Flushes pending compressed output to file. Only permitted on writing streams. If flush==Z_FINISH, completes the current gzip member; subsequent writes start a new member.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
flush is as in deflate() (e.g., Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FINISH).
Returns a zlib error code (gzerror() can be used for details).
Excessive flushing degrades compression.

functions.name: gzrewind
functions.description: Rewinds a gzFile opened for reading to the beginning (equivalent to (int)gzseek(file, 0, SEEK_SET)).
requirements: Supported only for reading.
Returns 0 on success (per gztell/gzseek conventions via cast).

functions.name: gzeof
functions.description: Returns non-zero if end-of-file indicator was set while reading, zero otherwise. EOF is set only when a read attempts past end of input.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
After gzeof() is true, reads return no data unless gzclearerr() is called and input has grown since last EOF.

functions.name: gzdirect
functions.description: Indicates whether reading is direct copy (not gzip) or, when writing, whether transparent writing was requested.
requirements: When used immediately after gzopen/gzdopen(), it will allocate buffers to probe header; call gzbuffer() before gzdirect() if changing buffer size.
For non-blocking or concurrently written inputs, may change from true to false once enough bytes (4) establish a gzip header.
When writing, reflects whether "wT" was specified.

functions.name: gzclose
functions.description: Flushes pending output if needed, closes the underlying file, and deallocates the gzFile state. Must not be called more than once for the same gzFile.
requirements: After closing, gzerror() must not be called since structures are freed.
Returns Z_STREAM_ERROR if invalid, Z_ERRNO on file error, Z_MEM_ERROR on OOM, Z_BUF_ERROR if last read ended mid gzip member, or Z_OK on success.

functions.name: gzclose_r
functions.description: Like gzclose(), but only for reading streams; avoids linking compression code in static builds.
requirements: Use only on reading streams. Same return codes as gzclose().

functions.name: gzclose_w
functions.description: Like gzclose(), but only for writing/appending streams; avoids linking decompression code in static builds.
requirements: Use only on writing/appending streams. Same return codes as gzclose().

functions.name: gzerror
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a string describing the last zlib-related error for file and sets *errnum to the zlib error number (Z_ERRNO for OS errors).
requirements: The returned string must not be modified; it may be invalidated by the next gzerror() call or by gzclose().
If file is closed, previously returned strings are no longer valid.
If errnum != NULL, *errnum is set.

functions.name: gzclearerr
functions.description: Clears the error and end-of-file indicators on file, analogous to clearerr() for stdio.
requirements: Use on a valid gzFile to continue reading after EOF on a concurrently written file.

functions.name: adler32
functions.signature: uLong adler32(uLong adler, const Bytef *buf, uInt len);
functions.description: Updates an Adler-32 checksum with len bytes from buf, returning the new checksum. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial value for a new checksum.
requirements: adler is the starting checksum (use 0 and buf=Z_NULL,len=0 to initialize).
buf may be Z_NULL only to request the initial value; otherwise must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: adler32_z
functions.signature: uLong adler32_z(uLong adler, const Bytef *buf, z_size_t len);
functions.description: Same as adler32(), but takes length as z_size_t.
requirements: Same as adler32(), with len as z_size_t.

functions.name: crc32
functions.signature: uLong crc32(uLong crc, const Bytef *buf, uInt len);
functions.description: Updates a CRC-32 checksum with len bytes from buf, returning the new checksum. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial CRC value (pre/post conditioning handled internally).
requirements: crc is the starting CRC (use 0 and buf=Z_NULL,len=0 to initialize).
buf may be Z_NULL only to request the initial value; otherwise must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: crc32_z
functions.signature: uLong crc32_z(uLong crc, const Bytef *buf, z_size_t len);
functions.description: Same as crc32(), but takes length as z_size_t.
requirements: Same as crc32(), with len as z_size_t.

functions.name: crc32_combine_op
functions.signature: uLong crc32_combine_op(uLong crc1, uLong crc2, uLong op);
functions.description: Combines two CRC-32 values crc1 and crc2 using a precomputed operator op (generated from len2 by crc32_combine_gen()). Faster for repeated combinations with the same len2.
requirements: op must be the operator derived from the concatenation length (len2) via crc32_combine_gen().
crc1 and crc2 are CRC-32 values computed with zlib’s crc32.

functions.name: deflateInit_
functions.signature: int deflateInit_(z_streamp strm, int level, const char *version, int stream_size);
functions.description: Versioned initializer for deflate streams (used by deflateInit macro). Sets up internal state; initializes totals, adler, and msg.
requirements: strm must not be NULL; strm->zalloc/zfree/opaque must be set or Z_NULL to use defaults.
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or 0..9.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must equal sizeof(z_stream).
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_STREAM_ERROR for invalid level, or Z_VERSION_ERROR on version/size mismatch.

functions.name: inflateInit_
functions.signature: int inflateInit_(z_streamp strm, const char *version, int stream_size);
functions.description: Versioned initializer for inflate streams (used by inflateInit macro). Defers window allocation until needed; initializes totals/adler/msg.
requirements: strm must not be NULL; next_in/avail_in may be set but not consumed here; zalloc/zfree/opaque set or default.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must equal sizeof(z_stream).
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_VERSION_ERROR, or Z_STREAM_ERROR for invalid parameters.

functions.name: deflateInit2_
functions.signature: int deflateInit2_(z_streamp strm, int level, int method, int windowBits, int memLevel, int strategy, const char *version, int stream_size);
functions.description: Extended deflate initializer with method, windowBits, memLevel, strategy, and optional raw/gzip modes. Used by deflateInit2 macro.
requirements: strm->zalloc/zfree/opaque initialized or Z_NULL for defaults.
method must be Z_DEFLATED.
windowBits normally 8..15 (8 becomes 9); negative for raw; add 16 for gzip wrapper; >15 for gzip; 256-byte window rejected for raw/gzip.
memLevel 1..9 (default 8).
strategy one of Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, Z_FILTERED, Z_RLE, Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY, Z_FIXED.
version==ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size==sizeof(z_stream).
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid params, or Z_VERSION_ERROR on version mismatch.

functions.name: inflateInit2_
functions.signature: int inflateInit2_(z_streamp strm, int windowBits, const char *version, int stream_size);
functions.description: Extended inflate initializer with windowBits and header mode control (raw, gzip, or auto detect). Used by inflateInit2 macro.
requirements: strm->next_in/avail_in, zalloc/zfree/opaque initialized (not consumed here).
windowBits: 8..15, 0 to use header value, negative for raw, 15+32 for zlib/gzip auto, 15+16 for gzip only.
Must be >= windowBits used by deflate, or equal to 15 if deflateInit2() not used.
version==ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size==sizeof(z_stream).
Returns Z_OK, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_VERSION_ERROR, or Z_STREAM_ERROR.

functions.name: inflateBackInit_
functions.signature: int inflateBackInit_(z_streamp strm, int windowBits, unsigned char *window, const char *version, int stream_size);
functions.description: Initializes a stream for callback-based raw inflation via inflateBack(), using caller-supplied window buffer. Used by inflateBackInit macro.
requirements: strm->zalloc/zfree/opaque set or defaults used if Z_NULL.
windowBits in 8..15; for general streams, use 15 and a 32K window.
window must point to a buffer of size 1<<windowBits.
version==ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size==sizeof(z_stream).
Returns Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR (invalid params), Z_MEM_ERROR (allocation failure), or Z_VERSION_ERROR.

functions.name: gzgetc_
functions.description: Backward-compatibility function that reads one byte from a gzFile (older symbol used by the gzgetc macro).
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
Returns byte [0..255] or -1 on EOF/error.

functions.name: gzopen
functions.description: Opens a file path for gzip-format reading (decompress) or writing (compress), with mode similar to fopen plus gzip options.
requirements: mode must include 'r', 'w', or 'a'; '+' is invalid. Optional: compression level digits (w), strategy flags (f,h,R,F), 'T' (transparent write/append), 'G' (disable transparent read), 'N' (non-blocking), 'e' (close-on-exec).
Returns NULL on open failure (check errno), invalid mode, or allocation failure. In 'N' mode, open may fail to avoid blocking (errno EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK).

functions.name: gzseek
functions.signature: z_off_t gzseek(gzFile file, z_off_t offset, int whence);
functions.description: Sets the position for the next gzread/gzwrite relative to whence, where offset counts uncompressed bytes. SEEK_END not supported.
requirements: SEEK on reading is emulated and can be very slow; on writing only forward seeks are supported (zeros are compressed to advance).
Any actual seeking is deferred until next read/write (or close when writing).
Returns new uncompressed offset from start, or -1 on error (e.g., backward seek on write).

functions.name: gztell
functions.description: Returns the current uncompressed offset for the next gzread/gzwrite (bytes from start).
requirements: Equivalent to gzseek(file, 0, SEEK_CUR).

functions.name: gzoffset
functions.description: Returns the current compressed-file offset, including any bytes before the gzip stream. Excludes unread buffered input when reading.
requirements: Returns -1 on error.

functions.name: adler32_combine
functions.signature: uLong adler32_combine(uLong adler1, uLong adler2, z_off_t len2);
functions.description: Combines two Adler-32 checksums adler1 and adler2 for concatenated sequences, given len2 (length of the second sequence).
requirements: len2 must be provided as the (signed) length of the second sequence; negative len2 yields meaningless results.

functions.name: crc32_combine
functions.signature: uLong crc32_combine(uLong crc1, uLong crc2, z_off_t len2);
functions.description: Combines two CRC-32 values for concatenated sequences, given len2 (length of the second sequence).
requirements: len2 must be non-negative.

functions.name: crc32_combine_gen
functions.description: Generates a reusable operator corresponding to len2 for use with crc32_combine_op().
requirements: len2 must be non-negative.

functions.name: zError
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for a given zlib error code.
requirements: Pass a zlib error code such as Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR, etc. Returned const string must not be modified.

functions.name: inflateSyncPoint
functions.description: Undocumented here; traditionally reports whether inflate is at a point that can be used for sync. Not part of the main API docs.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Behavior and return codes are undocumented; use with caution.

functions.name: get_crc_table
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal CRC-32 lookup table used by zlib. Undocumented/low-level utility.
requirements: Return is a const pointer; do not modify table contents.

functions.name: inflateUndermine
functions.description: Undocumented testing/diagnostic hook that relaxes inflate checking in some builds. Not for production use.
requirements: Use only in controlled/testing scenarios; parameters and effects are undocumented.

functions.name: inflateValidate
functions.description: Undocumented control to enable/disable validation checks during inflate. Not part of stable public API.
requirements: strm must be valid; second parameter toggles behavior; specifics are undocumented.

functions.name: inflateCodesUsed
functions.description: Returns an internal statistic: number of inflate codes used. Undocumented/diagnostic.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.

functions.name: inflateResetKeep
functions.description: Like inflateReset but retains allocated window and possibly other state. Undocumented here but commonly used to reset without freeing workspace.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream. Returns zlib status code (Z_OK on success).

functions.name: deflateResetKeep
functions.description: Like deflateReset but keeps allocated data structures to avoid reinitialization overhead. Undocumented here but analogous to inflateResetKeep.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream. Returns zlib status code (Z_OK on success).

functions.name: gzvprintf
functions.signature: int gzvprintf(gzFile file, const char *format, va_list va);
functions.description: vfprintf-like variant of gzprintf that formats using a va_list, compresses, and writes to gzFile. Returns number of uncompressed bytes written or negative error code.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
Subject to same size limits as gzprintf (buffer and 8191-bytes default cap unless gzbuffer() increased).
va_list must be valid for the format string.

data_types.description: A generic byte buffer that may contain any sequence of bytes (0x00–0xFF), not required to be valid text or to follow any specific format. Used for raw input, compressed data, dictionaries, checksums, and general binary payloads.
A byte sequence intended to be interpreted as a C string, terminated by a NUL (0x00) byte. Contents before the terminator may be arbitrary bytes but typically represent text.

A short human-readable text string suitable for formatted output functions. Typically composed of printable ASCII/UTF-8 characters without embedded NULs; does not require a trailing NUL when passed alongside explicit length or via std::string::c_str() which adds one.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List

# This generator targets zlib fuzz stubs that request arbitrary binary buffers
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We provide valid/interesting
# binary data covering:
# - Reasonable deflate dictionaries (<= 32 KiB)
# - Valid gzip/zlib members of varying sizes and properties
# - Raw deflate streams
# - Data likely to trigger Z_NEED_DICT (by compressing with a dictionary)
# - Buffers for checksum APIs (random, repetitive, zeroes, incremental bytes)
# - Small headers and blocks useful for inflateSync (contains 00 00 FF FF)
# - Filenames as bytes (the harness maps to a filename pointing to a buffer)
# The output is a single bytes blob; the fuzzing framework will slice it to
# feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls across stubs.

MAX_OUT = 4096

def _rnd(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_repeats(r: random.Random, unit_len: int, total: int) -> bytes:
    unit = _rnd(r, unit_len)
    reps = max(1, total // max(1, unit_len))
    data = (unit * reps)[:total]
    return data

def _make_dictionary(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a compact, useful dictionary of length 1..32768
    # Mix common ASCII, repeated substrings, and random noise.
    target = r.randint(64, 32768)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Common text tokens
    tokens = [
        b"GET /index.html HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n",
        b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. ",
        b"User-Agent: fuzz/1.0\r\n",
        b"Content-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n",
        b"\x00\x00\xff\xff",  # inflateSync marker
    ]
    r.shuffle(tokens)
    for t in tokens:
        chunks.append(t)
        if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) > target // 2:
            break
    # Add repeated patterns and random tails
    chunks.append(_pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(3, 16), r.randint(64, 512)))
    chunks.append(_rnd(r, r.randint(32, 256)))
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) < target:
        data += _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(4, 32), target - len(data))
    return data[:target]

def _gzip_member(r: random.Random, payload: bytes, mtime: int = None, name: bytes | None = None, comment: bytes | None = None, add_hcrc: bool = False) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal gzip member by hand to control header features
    # Format per RFC 1952
    ID1, ID2 = 0x1f, 0x8b
    CM = 8  # deflate
    FLG_FTEXT = 0x01
    FLG_FHCRC = 0x02
    FLG_FEXTRA = 0x04
    FLG_FNAME = 0x08
    FLG_FCOMMENT = 0x10
    flg = 0
    # We won't add EXTRA to keep things compact
    if name is not None: flg |= FLG_FNAME
    if comment is not None: flg |= FLG_FCOMMENT
    if add_hcrc: flg |= FLG_FHCRC
    if mtime is None:
        mtime = r.randint(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    XFL = 0
    OS = r.randrange(0, 255)
    header = bytearray([ID1, ID2, CM, flg])
    header += struct.pack('<I', mtime)
    header += bytes([XFL, OS])
    if name is not None:
        header += name.replace(b"\x00", b" ") + b"\x00"
    if comment is not None:
        header += comment.replace(b"\x00", b" ") + b"\x00"
    if add_hcrc:
        # CRC16 of header so far
        crc16 = zlib.crc32(bytes(header)) & 0xFFFF
        header += struct.pack('<H', crc16)
    # Deflate payload (zlib wants raw deflate via wbits=-15, but gzip member uses raw deflate inside)
    comp = zlib.compress(payload)  # zlib wrapper
    # Strip zlib header and adler32 to obtain raw deflate stream
    # zlib header is 2 bytes (or 3/4 if preset dictionary, which we do not use here)
    # We'll attempt robust stripping by using wbits=31 to get gzip, but we need raw; instead, re-compress raw.
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=r.randint(1, 9), wbits=-15).compress(payload) + zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=-15).flush()
    # Trailer: CRC32 and ISIZE
    crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    isize = len(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    trailer = struct.pack('<II', crc, isize)
    return bytes(header) + comp + trailer

def _zlib_stream(r: random.Random, payload: bytes, with_dict: bytes | None = None) -> bytes:
    # Create a zlib-wrapped deflate stream. Optionally use a preset dictionary to provoke NEED_DICT on inflate.
    if with_dict is None:
        return zlib.compress(payload)
    # Use preset dictionary
    cobj = zlib.compressobj(level=r.randint(1, 9), wbits=15)
    try:
        cobj.set_dictionary(with_dict)
    except Exception:
        # If dict too large, zlib may still accept but keep only window size; ensure <= 32K
        pass
    comp = cobj.compress(payload) + cobj.flush()
    return comp

def _raw_deflate(r: random.Random, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    cobj = zlib.compressobj(level=r.randint(1, 9), wbits=-15)
    return cobj.compress(payload) + cobj.flush()

def _inflate_sync_candidate(r: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    # Include 00 00 FF FF marker to allow inflateSync to succeed sometimes
    pre = _rnd(r, max(0, total - 8))
    return pre + b"\x00\x00\xff\xff" + _rnd(r, 4)

def _compose_blobs(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    blobs: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Dictionary blob (<= 32K, non-empty)
    dict_blob = _make_dictionary(r)
    blobs.append(dict_blob)

    # 2) Small plain data (for adler32/crc32 and gzwrite)
    small_plain = _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(2, 8), r.randint(32, 256))
    blobs.append(small_plain)

    # 3) Valid zlib stream without dictionary
    payload1 = _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(3, 32), r.randint(64, 512))
    blobs.append(_zlib_stream(r, payload1))

    # 4) Valid zlib stream with preset dictionary to trigger NEED_DICT on inflate
    payload2 = _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(4, 16), r.randint(64, 512))
    # Use a trimmed dictionary (<= 32K)
    dict2 = dict_blob[: min(len(dict_blob), 32768)]
    blobs.append(_zlib_stream(r, payload2, with_dict=dict2))

    # 5) Valid gzip member with optional name/comment/hcrc
    name = b"file_" + _rnd(r, r.randint(3, 8))
    comment = b"note:" + _rnd(r, r.randint(3, 12))
    gz_payload = _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(2, 12), r.randint(32, 400))
    blobs.append(_gzip_member(r, gz_payload, name=name, comment=comment, add_hcrc=r.choice([False, True])))

    # 6) Raw deflate stream
    raw_payload = _pattern_repeats(r, r.randint(2, 16), r.randint(64, 400))
    blobs.append(_raw_deflate(r, raw_payload))

    # 7) InflateSync candidate containing 00 00 FF FF
    blobs.append(_inflate_sync_candidate(r, r.randint(16, 128)))

    # 8) Checksums-specific buffers: zeros, incremental, random
    blobs.append(b"\x00" * r.randint(16, 128))
    blobs.append(bytes(range(0, 256)))
    blobs.append(_rnd(r, r.randint(32, 256)))

    # 9) Minimal non-empty strings for name/comment zero-termination scenarios
    blobs.append(b"A\x00")
    blobs.append(b"Comment\x00")

    return blobs

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Compose multiple valid blobs separated by size-prefixed framing, so the harness can slice deterministically
    blobs = _compose_blobs(r)

    # Also interleave some length-prefixed slices to assist stubs that expect multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    out = bytearray()
    for b in blobs:
        if len(out) + 4 + len(b) > MAX_OUT:
            break
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(b) & 0xFFFF)
        # Add a simple type tag to diversify (0=zlib,1=gzip,2=raw,3=dict,4=misc) guessed by heuristics
        tag = 3 if len(b) == len(blobs[0]) else 1 if b[:2] == b"\x1f\x8b" else 0 if len(b) >= 2 and b[0] & 0x0f == 8 else 2 if b[:2] not in (b"\x1f\x8b",) and len(b) > 10 else 4
        out += bytes([tag])
        out += b
    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(_rnd(r, min(64, MAX_OUT)))
    return bytes(out[:MAX_OUT])

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: null-terminated string
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME().
# We will generate a bytes blob containing several null-terminated strings laid out
# sequentially, so that successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls pull interesting values.
# For FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(), many harnesses map it to a temp path referencing this
# buffer. We therefore include plausible path-like strings as well.
#
# Stubs of interest:
# - deflateSetHeader: wants strings for gzip header fields: extra (binary ok), name (must be NUL-terminated), comment (NUL-terminated).
# - inflateGetHeader: provides buffers for extra/name/comment; again NUL-terminated helpful.
# - gzputs: writes a null-terminated string; should be valid C string without embedded NULs before terminator.
# - gzopen: uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to open a path, and a valid mode selected internally.
#
# Strategy:
# Generate a sequence of null-terminated payloads including:
# - Filenames/paths that are likely valid on POSIX and Windows (relative and absolute forms).
# - Gzip-friendly names/comments (ASCII and UTF-8), varying sizes including edge cases.
# - Binary "extra" fields up to 128 bytes (can include any bytes; we will still NUL-terminate as a C-string provider).
# - Some long strings near limits used in stubs (64, 128, 512) to exercise truncation.
# - Ensure the overall buffer size <= 4096.
# - Randomize selection and ordering with the seed.

SAFE_ASCII = (
    "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    "0123456789"
    " .-_+@#%()[]{}!$^&=,;"  # avoid wildcard/shell metachars like * ? | > < to keep paths usable
)

UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "naïve",
    "café",
    "😀",
    "日本語",
    "файл",
    "münchen",
    "παράδειγμα",
    "مرحبا",
]

POSIX_ROOTS = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm", "/tmp/.", "/"]
WIN_DRIVES = ["C:", "D:"]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    base = r.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
    # Mix with safe ascii to vary lengths while keeping valid UTF-8
    pad = _rand_ascii(r, max(0, min_len - len(base)), max(0, max_len - len(base)))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return base + pad
    else:
        return pad + base


def _path_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []
    # Relative simple names
    for ext in ["", ".gz", ".txt", ".log", ".data"]:
        cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 12) + ext)
    # Nested relative paths
    for _ in range(2):
        parts = [_rand_ascii(r, 1, 6) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4))]
        cands.append("/".join(parts) + r.choice(["", ".gz", ".txt"]))
    # POSIX absolute
    for root in POSIX_ROOTS:
        name = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 10)
        cands.append(f"{root.rstrip('/')}/{name}.gz")
    # Windows-like paths (use backslashes)
    for d in WIN_DRIVES:
        name = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 10)
        cands.append(f"{d}\\\
{name}.gz")
    # Edge cases
    cands.append("-")  # some tools use '-' as stdin/stdout, useful for rejection paths too
    cands.append(".hidden.gz")
    return cands


def _gzip_name_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 10))
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 20, 40))  # longer name
    cands.append(_rand_utf8(r, 3, 20))
    # Names similar to filenames
    cands.extend([p.split("/")[-1] for p in _path_candidates(r) if p])
    # Boundary sizes around 64 (stub truncates name to 64 before adding terminator)
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 60, 64))
    cands.append(_rand_utf8(r, 60, 64))
    return cands


def _gzip_comment_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []
    cands.append("generated by fuzz harness")
    cands.append(_rand_utf8(r, 10, 40))
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 100, 128))
    cands.append(_rand_utf8(r, 120, 128))
    # Very short and empty
    cands.append("")
    cands.append("OK")
    return cands


def _gzip_extra_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    cands: List[bytes] = []
    # ID/subfield style: 2-byte ID, 2-byte length, payload
    for _ in range(3):
        sid1 = r.randint(0, 255)
        sid2 = r.randint(0, 255)
        payload = r.randbytes(r.randint(0, 32))
        sub = bytes([sid1, sid2]) + struct.pack("<H", len(payload)) + payload
        # wrap in total length field as per gzip extra layout when multiple subs (optional)
        cands.append(sub)
    # Random binary up to 128
    cands.append(r.randbytes(r.randint(0, 128)))
    # Textual extra (still binary allowed)
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 5, 30).encode("ascii"))
    return cands


def _gzputs_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []
    # Typical lines
    cands.append("hello world")
    cands.append("a" * 80)
    cands.append(_rand_utf8(r, 10, 60))
    # Near 512 limit used in stub (it truncates input to 512 before passing)
    cands.append(_rand_ascii(r, 480, 512))
    # Include newlines and format-like content (gzprintf-like patterns) though gzputs just writes raw
    cands.append("line1\nline2\n")
    cands.append("%s %d %% done")
    return cands


def _nt(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure a single NUL terminator and avoid internal NULs when meant as C-strings.
    # For binary extras, internal NULs are fine; we still append a terminator for provider API.
    return s + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Filename candidates for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME()
    paths = _path_candidates(r)
    r.shuffle(paths)
    for p in paths[:r.randint(3, 7)]:
        # Keep ASCII, avoid embedded NULs
        pb = p.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        # Ensure non-empty
        if not pb:
            pb = b"file.gz"
        chunks.append(_nt(pb))

    # 2) gzip name/comment candidates for deflateSetHeader/inflateGetHeader
    names = _gzip_name_candidates(r)
    comments = _gzip_comment_candidates(r)
    r.shuffle(names)
    r.shuffle(comments)
    for s in names[:r.randint(3, 6)]:
        nb = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        # Ensure no internal NULs for C-string semantics
        nb = nb.replace(b"\x00", b"")
        chunks.append(_nt(nb))
    for s in comments[:r.randint(3, 6)]:
        cb = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore").replace(b"\x00", b"")
        chunks.append(_nt(cb))

    # 3) gzip extra fields (binary allowed)
    extras = _gzip_extra_candidates(r)
    r.shuffle(extras)
    for e in extras[:r.randint(2, 5)]:
        # As provider of null-terminated strings, append NUL to delimit; internal NULs remain
        chunks.append(_nt(e))

    # 4) gzputs() payloads
    gzs = _gzputs_strings(r)
    r.shuffle(gzs)
    for s in gzs[:r.randint(3, 6)]:
        sb = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore").replace(b"\x00", b"")
        chunks.append(_nt(sb))

    # 5) Additional small random ASCII strings for general consumption by FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        s = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 32)
        chunks.append(_nt(s.encode("ascii")))

    # Assemble, ensuring max total size <= 4096
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4095]  # ensure we have room to add final terminator
        # Ensure last byte is NUL-terminated; find last NUL or append
        if not out.endswith(b"\x00"):
            out = out + b"\x00"
    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Provide initial buffers for a fuzzer stub that exercises gzprintf on a writable gzFile.
# The stub uses:
#  - FUZZ_GET_ATTR_STR(file, "mode") and requires it to be exactly "w"
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as a short printable string (trimmed to 64 by the stub)
#  - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) as an integer value to format
#
# Many fuzzing harnesses multiplex inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_* calls from a single bytestream using
# simple length-prefixed segments. We'll generate a compact, self-describing buffer encoding:
#   [mode]\0 [string_len][string_bytes] [uint32_le]
# Where:
#   - mode is a C string for file mode, must be "w" to pass the stub's predicate.
#   - string_len is one byte 0..64, limiting size in the stub anyway.
#   - string_bytes are printable ASCII (no embedded NUL).
#   - uint32_le is the value for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# This makes the buffer likely valid regardless of the exact harness, while being simple to parse.
# The returned buffer is <= 4096 bytes.

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '


def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Prefer common readable words interspersed with punctuation to explore formatting paths
    # while remaining printable. Avoid NULs; ensure bytes are ASCII.
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    chars = [rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n)]
    s = ''.join(chars)
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces collapsing in some consumers; keep as-is otherwise
    return s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')


def _biased_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward interesting sizes for gzprintf: small, boundary, and max(64)
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 31, 32, 63, 64]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    # Otherwise any value 0..64
    return rng.randint(0, 64)


def _biased_uint32(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Provide corner-case integers and random ones
    interesting = [0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 127, 128, 255, 256, 1024, 4096,
                   2**15-1, 2**15, 2**16-1, 2**16, 2**31-1, 2**31, 2**32-1]
    if rng.random() < 0.65:
        return rng.choice(interesting) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return rng.getrandbits(32)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Mode must be exactly "w" for the stub; occasionally add flags commonly accepted by zlib
    # but keep the first char 'w'. However, the stub checks strcmp(mode, "w") == 0, so only "w" passes.
    mode = b"w\x00"

    # Printable string segment
    slen = _biased_lengths(rng)
    sbytes = _rand_printable(rng, slen)

    # Unsigned int parameter (little-endian 4 bytes)
    u = _biased_uint32(rng)
    uint_le = bytes((u & 0xFF, (u >> 8) & 0xFF, (u >> 16) & 0xFF, (u >> 24) & 0xFF))

    # Assemble: mode\0, 1-byte length, string, uint32_le
    out = bytearray()
    out += mode              # "w\0"
    out.append(slen & 0xFF)  # length for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    out += sbytes            # printable string bytes
    out += uint_le           # FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)

    return bytes(out)
